verdict.rationale: Muse lets users name and shape their avatar's personality/tone (muse-docs-17, muse-docs-2) and persists memory about the user across sessions, which can be edited or selectively forgotten (muse-supp-vm-files-export, muse-docs-12). However, there is no evidence of an explicit 'custom instructions' or system-prompt-style setting that a power-user can write once to durably govern all future responses beyond persona/tone. Missing for 10: a documented settings field for persistent behavioral instructions/preferences, evidence that such instructions apply across all interaction modes (WhatsApp, Mac, mobile), and independent confirmation that memory-driven customization actually shapes every response consistently.
